among the verses of Aeschylus he has this, which the scholiast explains as διὰ τοῦ ἀέρος φοιτώσαις [going through the air]. The verse is perhaps taken from the Sphinx, from which a similar verse is cited there at 1287 (fr. 234). κύνας ἀεροφοίτους [air-wandering dogs] he calls the eagles, as in Prom. 1020 and Agam. 139.
